While not as important as batting, bowling and technique, fielding has a definite influence over the number of runs your opponent is able to score, and also the number of wicket taking opportunities your team is able to generate. Generation of runout opportunities is closely linked to the comparative fielding abilities of the two teams in a match, with the better fielding team being more likely to create runout opportunities. Fielding is also of some importance to your wicketkeeper, although not nearly as important as his keeping skill.  Safe Hands    Receives a bonus to any fielding or wicketkeeping related skill check during a match.

[2019-02-14 22:19] butlee : I think you’d give them advice on what to go for
[2019-02-14 22:20] butlee : Sort of how much risk they’d play for and which parts of their game to make the most of (or take more risks on those parts)
[2019-02-14 22:22] butlee : So if it were windy (across the course) off a tee shot for example, the player would use his instructions mixed with mental skills to decide how wide to factor his shot. And then his skills (including specific skills with that club) to make the shot.

[2019-02-14 22:24] butlee : So you’d still give ‘orders’ to some degree, but it was a lot more focused on the preparation of your golfers and the match day experience was more about the viewing pleasure.

[2019-08-09 03:20] _deltronzero : They are created based on scheduled match times and not the actual running of the games. The games run in the background with a scheduled finish time which is when the ratings become available. Commentary has a time stamp on it and the game only displays commentary that is less than the current game time. Games not running is usually as a result of match orders not meeting the required parameters and the game locks up as it processes them one after the other.
[2019-08-09 03:22] .werdo64 : Thanks DZ.
[2019-08-09 03:38] _deltronzero : There are also 2 process for the matches. The batch process for all games in a div/country and the clean up process which runs every 5 minutes to miss those. The clean up processes are the ones running the games at the moment.

[2019-09-11 04:04] .werdo64 : <@236698087739883520> I think the best answer they can give is this: Technologically speaking, all things are possible (though not all are practical). Ash wrote the game (all aspects) in common languages (HTML, CSS, JAVASCRIPT, JAVA, PHP, SQL) of which  there are many developers. As such, making changes to any aspect of the game is very possible. The key is that every person's programming style is unique (like handwriting) so some changes will be easy to implement, and others will take a bit more time as they learn not only the code, but also Ash's style of the code. They will also slowly learn, as they read more of the code, and get up to speed with Ash's style, how each of the pieces bolts together, and reference each other. This will then allow them to, with better speed and accuracy, implement changes or advise if a change just isn't going to suit the calculations. (e.g. Bowler delivery speed. Many people asked for this, but it would have just been a visual representation with no actual influence on the ball calculations, cause of the way the ME was written). When the team finally got access to the game, they encountered issue after issue that meant they were simply putting out 'spot fires' rather than being able to dig into the code of the game and explore how far they could go. First there were stability issues (all those probably stem back to the eventual issues that have brought the game down this time, requiring this downtime and rebuild time, but that was almost impossible to have determined beforehand). AND then they needed to prepare for EOS. The EOS preparation required looking into specific parts of the code, and commands that had previously been executed to establish an approx. order of operations, in the case that later processes required earlier ones to be run to complete successfully.
[2019-09-11 04:04] .werdo64 : Once they got through EOS successfully they were about to begin the process I outlined above of digging into the code to see what was easily possible to get some quick wins(W & NB's), and what would require more in-depth coding and testing. So in each of the current management teams responses there has been a mix of optimism and reality.  Optimism because they know technically it can be done. Reality because they know it will be a hard road, and in some cases while it 'could' be done, it realistically wont.
